original_test_intent: Read the selected BMC Manager's EthernetInterfaces collection and produce an accurate inventory of management network interfaces without changing network state.
original_method: Resolve the advertised EthernetInterfaces collection from a validated Manager, issue one trusted GET, validate collection identity/count/member links, summarize safe operational fields and redact network topology identifiers.
manual_activity: Provide read-only BMC access, CA trust, firmware schema and the approved handling policy for MAC/IP/VLAN/hostname evidence; no network change is required.
required_inputs: Managers collection membership and advertised EthernetInterfaces link
safety_requirements: Never PATCH, POST or follow network actions
Validate Manager and same-origin collection link
Do not infer reachability or management role from names alone
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager and firmware identity
Capture HTTP metadata and restricted raw hash
Validate collection type, count and member array
Validate unique canonical same-origin member links under the selected Manager
Summarize member IDs and safe status metadata
Confirm no network/log state change occurred
engineer_actions: Provide any mandatory interface inventory and redaction policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The GET matches collection retrieval, but `-k`, embedded credentials, log clearing, unredacted full JSON and readability-only acceptance are unsafe and incomplete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the Manager's advertised collection URI for one trusted GET, validate count and canonical member links, redact topology identifiers and prohibit all action/write traversal.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager EthernetInterfaces GET and 15/10 timing remain; no Manager instance, expected member count or interface role is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate the collection as an identity graph and export only the network fields authorized by the evidence policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes evidence clearing and insecure/raw capture, adding Manager linkage, internal consistency, same-origin membership and topology privacy.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers interface inventory only; it does not prove link traffic, routing, failover or configuration mutation behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A valid collection can include disabled or service-only interfaces and cannot by itself establish which path carries the agent's management session.

project_override_considerations: Project-supplied expected interfaces should be matched by stable identity or approved role mapping, not array order or assumed names. Preserve restricted raw hashes when exported values are redacted.
expected_evidence: HTTP status/content type/timing and restricted raw hash
Collection identity, member count and unique canonical links
Proof no network/configuration action or log clear occurred

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, displayed path and GET all identify the Manager EthernetInterfaces collection. Unsafe setup and weak criteria do not create an alternate source identity.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Normal identity, access, schema and redaction inputs are sufficient for deterministic read-only collection automation.

review_improvement: Changes a sensitive raw network dump into a Manager-bound, internally consistent and privacy-controlled collection inventory.
independent_technical_reasoning: The collection is useful only when every member belongs to the selected Manager and its count agrees with unique canonical links. A successful GET does not establish that, and it may expose the BMC's management topology. Redaction must protect addresses and VLAN/hostname information while retaining stable member identity, operational status and a restricted raw hash for audit. Since all checks are bounded and read-only and no physical or discretionary step is inherent, the case remains fully automatable.
